name: Kunsthalle Mannheim
known: Opened in 1909 as a municipal art gallery under its first director Fritz Wichert, in a building designed by Hermann Billing for an international art exhibition in 1907 (Wikipedia; the museum).
Directors have included Gustav Friedrich Hartlaub, who coined the term "New Objectivity" for a 1925 exhibition and was dismissed by the Nazis in 1933, and Ulrike Lorenz.
The Art Newspaper describes Hector as one of the founders of the software company SAP; its headline calls him a German billionaire.

Stiftung Kunsthalle Mannheim, founded in 2012, has a foundation council chaired by Susanne Fuchs that includes Mannheim's Lord Mayor Christian Specht and Culture Mayor Thorsten Riehle; its executive board is Luisa Heese (chair) and Christoph Geber (finance).

name: Die Neue Sammlung - The Design Museum
known: From 1934, under the Nazi regime, the museum, described as "nicht konform agierende" (not acting in conformity), was placed under the general directorate of the Bayerisches Nationalmuseum.
Angelika Nollert has been director since May 2014.

name: Haus der Kunst
known: A Bavarian ministry official chairs its supervisory board. 2024 attendance was nearly 440,000.

name: Kunstverein München
known: Tom Engels is director (team page).
The City of Munich council paper of 18 September 2025 says Maurin Dietrich, director since 2019, was expected to leave at the end of 2025.
Rüdiger Maaß (chairman), Julie Schemann (vice chairwoman), Aileen Faustmann (treasurer), Dr.

name: Lothringer 13 Halle
known: Between 1980 and 1998 the city's culture department, guest curators and staff organised the exhibitions.
Since 1998 rotating independent curators have led the programme (German Wikipedia).
German Wikipedia states that Lisa Britzger became artistic director in 2020 and Kalas Liebfried took over as head in April 2025.

name: Museum Abteiberg
known: Directors since: Dierk Stemmler (1985 to 1994), Veit Loers (1995 to 2003) and Susanne Titz (since 2004) (Wikipedia).

name: Kunsthalle Münster
known: Opened on 19 September 1991 as the municipal Ausstellungshalle am Hawerkamp under its first director Gail B.

The Kunsthalle hosts Residence NRW+, begun in 2020: four 12-month scholarships a year for visual artists up to age 40 with ties to NRW at EUR 1,450 a month, and four 6-month scholarships for curators up to age 35 at EUR 1,250 a month.

name: Kunsthalle Recklinghausen
known: Förderverein für Bildende Kunst: a non-profit association, chaired by Dieter Delius, that can finance acquisitions and exhibitions and helps pay for the website; it also arranges grants, donations and sponsorship.

name: Akademie Schloss Solitude
known: Directors: Jean-Baptiste Joly (founding director until 2018), Elke aus dem Moore (until 2022), and Anne Fleckstein since February 2024 (German Wikipedia).

The Board of Trustees lists two members from the advisory board of Kunststiftung Baden-Württemberg, four members of the Landtag (AfD, Bündnis 90/Die Grünen, SPD, CDU) and the head of Stuttgart's Kulturamt (the Akademie's Foundation Bodies page, undated).

name: Künstlerhaus Stuttgart
known: Founded by Stuttgart artists in 1978 (stated by the Künstlerhaus;
The board is Ania Corcilius (first chairperson), Jochen Detscher (deputy) and Christoph Schwerdtfeger (treasurer).
Juliane Gebhardt is managing director.
Tamarind Rossetti and Stephen Wright have been artistic directors since 1 January 2024 (stated by the Künstlerhaus).

Earlier artistic directors include Ulrich Bernhardt (1978 to 1986), Veit Görner, Ute Meta Bauer, Nicolaus Schafhausen, Fareed Armaly, Elke aus dem Moore, Axel John Wieder, Adnan Yildiz, Fatima Hellberg (2015 to 2019) and Eric Golo Stone from 2020 (German Wikipedia).
Curatorial fellowships, public printing workshops, sound and video labs, experimental sculpture

name: Weissenhofmuseum im Haus Le Corbusier
known: The city was given the chance to buy the double house in 2002 and restored it with the Wüstenrot Stiftung and its conservation board; no cost or share is stated (museum's site).

name: Württembergischer Kunstverein Stuttgart
known: Its founders included the jurist and painter Carl Urban Keller.

name: Vitra Design Museum
known: Founded in 1989 by the Vitra company and Rolf Fehlbaum, son of Vitra's founders (museum website, Wikipedia).
Alexander von Vegesack was founding director from 1989 to 2010.
Mateo Kries has been director since 2020 (museum website).
IKEA Stiftung, founded by the German IKEA companies in 1981, backs the 2026 show.
